leetcodedataset.redistribute: converted I/O pairs only, with attribution
leetcodedataset.role: Seed hidden tests (STEP 4b-i): input_output pairs for LeetCode 743, 215, 28, 1, 287, 587, 509, 547, 300, 56, 347, 435, 684, 210, 34 (T02-T14 except T09/T12, R1-R3, R6); reference completions; topic tags.
leetcodedataset.caveats: No design-class problems: 146 (LRU, T09) and 295 (MedianFinder, T12) are absent, so their tests must be generated. Problem text is memorised by LLMs: reuse I/O only, never the wording.

mercury.role: Human-written LeetCode solutions (8-30 per target incl. 146 LRU and 295 median finder) as an external, mode-diverse program pool for the AST/tracer labellers and judge sanity checks (STEP 5); LeetCode metadata.
mercury.caveats: generator_code is the string 'None' for the bench targets (train split); a few solutions are LeetCode I/O hacks (sys.stdout/stdin) and must be filtered.

llm_creativity.redistribute: NO - evaluation only; never copy programs into published files
llm_creativity.role: T02 continuity: find_path(graph, start, goal) contract (lc/tasks.py), 225 claude-sonnet-5 programs (runs/T1/<strategy>/<i>/solution.py) with authoritative blind-judge labels (analysis/judge/T1/*.json) for the external labeller check (STEP 5); AST rules lc/rules.py as a reference pattern.
llm_creativity.caveats: negative_memory_v1_confounded (25 programs) is a confounded run the README excludes from the headline 200.

thealgorithms_python.role: Named textbook implementations for almost every catalogue mode (Dijkstra x4, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall x2, A*, bidirectional Dijkstra/BFS, 0-1 BFS, quickselect, median-of-medians, KMP, Rabin-Karp, Boyer-Moore(-Horspool), Z, naive search, Graham scan, Jarvis march, Fibonacci variants incl. fast doubling and matrix power, LIS O(n^2)/O(n log n), LRU, DSU, topological sort, binary/exponential search): starting points for references (STEP 4a) and an out-of-distribution test set for AST rules.
thealgorithms_python.caveats: Educational code: verify on hidden tests before use. Master targets Python 3.14: divide_and_conquer/convex_hull.py does not parse under 3.12.

clrs_text_test.role: Ground-truth execution traces of 30 CLRS algorithms (bfs, dfs, dijkstra, bellman_ford, floyd_warshall, dag_shortest_paths, quickselect, naive_string_matcher, kmp_matcher, graham_scan, jarvis_march, activity_selector, topological_sort, mst_kruskal, binary_search, ...) to unit-test the tracer's access-order features (STEP 5).
clrs_text_test.caveats: Text traces on small inputs (length 4-64); split test_1 only.

xlcost_python_program_level.role: GeeksforGeeks Python programs whose titles name the algorithm (69 Fibonacci incl. fast doubling, 12 LIS incl. N log N, quickselect, Boyer-Moore, Rabin-Karp, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, DSU, ...): extra out-of-distribution AST-rule checks and alias mining.
xlcost_python_program_level.caveats: Code is tokenised (NEW_LINE/INDENT/DEDENT); detokenise first. Repo ships a loader script, so data comes from refs/convert/parquet.

kodcode_light_rl_10k.role: LLM-written (GPT-4o), test-verified solutions to algorithm-named questions (Algorithm/Data_Structure/Leetcode subsets: 40 Dijkstra, 42 binary search, 23 Fibonacci, 17 BFS, 11 DFS, 9 Rabin-Karp, 8 topological ...): AST-rule checks on LLM-style code.
kodcode_light_rl_10k.caveats: Synthetic; labels come from question text, so treat as forced-implementation analogues, not ground truth.

rosetta_code.redistribute: GFDL copyleft; do not copy into the bench
rosetta_code.role: Independent Python implementations of named tasks (Dijkstra's algorithm, Floyd-Warshall, Quickselect, Longest increasing subsequence, Topological sort, Binary search, Fibonacci sequence): alias lists and judge/AST sanity items.
rosetta_code.caveats: One Python variant per task; 'Convex hull' uses shapely (third-party) and Fibonacci is the analytic variant only.

enamel.role: Expert efficient references + size-levelled input generators that separate sub-optimal from optimal algorithms (incl. HumanEval/55 fib, levels 10/30/9000/10000): template for the time-limit rule and stress-size calibration (STEP 4c).
enamel.caveats: HumanEval problems, not the bench tasks.

enamel_github.role: Companion to 'enamel': expert and canonical solution samples (samples/*.json) and the eff@k evaluator.

humanevalplus.role: Harness validation set: 164 canonical solutions with ~80x augmented tests must all pass through bench/harness/run_tests.py; Fibonacci-family tasks (HumanEval/39, 46, 55, 63, 130).

neocoder.role: Closest prior art for prohibition prompts (denial prompting): 199 Codeforces problems with progressive technique bans (for loop, if statement, while loop, recursion, hashmap, sorting, ...), human solutions with technique annotations, and annotated test cases.
neocoder.caveats: Bans are syntactic techniques, not algorithm modes; stdin programs.

creativityprism.role: Cross-domain creativity inputs (AUT alternative uses, TTCT, short stories) for testing whether seeding/temperature effects found on code transfer to divergent-thinking tasks; NeoCoder copy.
creativityprism.caveats: Peripheral to the coding bench; licence varies per task.

novelty_bench.role: 100 curated + 1,000 WildChat prompts that admit many distinct answers: non-code probe for the original request's temperature/top-k 'ideas vs phrasings' and context-seeding questions.
novelty_bench.caveats: Only the prompt files are downloaded (the 1.9 GB repo also holds evaluation results).

concreteness_ratings.licence: mit (mirror tag; original OSF norms licence not stated)
concreteness_ratings.paper: Brysbaert, Warriner & Kuperman 2014, Behavior Research Methods 46:904-911
concreteness_ratings.role: Neutral-twin noun bank and context-seed words (STEP 2 name-only/neutral twins; original request item 2): 39,954 lemmas with concreteness, SUBTLEX frequency and dominant POS; 996 concrete frequent nouns are single Qwen3 tokens.
concreteness_ratings.caveats: Filter offensive/body words before use (e.g. 'breasts' is in the concrete-frequent set).

open_english_wordnet_2023.paper: McCrae et al., Open English WordNet
open_english_wordnet_2023.role: Noun lexicographer files (noun.artifact/animal/plant/food vs noun.cognition/act/communication) to keep algorithm-like abstract nouns out of the neutral bank.
